He measured and photographed the unusual structure before contacting Lyson, a senior curator of vertebrate palaeontology at the Denver Museum of Nature & Science.At the time, scientists had identified only two adult T. rex footprints anywhere in the world, one in New Mexico and one in Montana, making the possibility of a third particularly significant.When Hups returned to the site the following day with companions, they identified another possible track. Lyson remained unconvinced and said he wanted to see a pattern. According to National Geographic's account of the discovery, Lyson marked a location where a third footprint should appear if the structures formed a genuine trackway. Excavation there revealed another footprint, followed by a fourth. The resulting sequence records two left and two right footprints. The published study titled A large tridactyl trackway from the Upper Cretaceous Hell Creek Formation of North Dakota, likely attributable to an adult Tyrannosaurus rex , describes the trackway as approximately 7 metres long, with the footprints each measuring roughly 1 metre in length. The distinction between an isolated footprint and a trackway is important. A single print can provide information about foot size and shape, but a sequence shows how an animal moved. In this case, the spacing between the prints gives researchers a stride of about 13 feet and allows them to estimate the dinosaur's walking speed.The discovery was made in the Hell Creek Formation of southwestern North Dakota, near Marmarth, on federal land administered by the U.S. Forest Service. The rocks formed about 66.5 million years ago in an environment that included forested floodplains, streams and swampy areas. The formation is particularly famous for dinosaur bones, including T. rex and Triceratops, but footprints are far rarer. The watery environment may help explain why. Sediment and flowing water could disturb or erase footprints before they became preserved. In this case, Lyson and his colleagues hypothesise that the three-toed depressions filled with warm, sandy water containing bacteria soon after the animal walked through. Sediments and minerals then accumulated in the hollows, eventually producing a dense mixture of calcium carbonate and sandstone around the footprints. Erosion later removed softer surrounding material and exposed the hardened structures.The resulting fossils are unusual because they are not simply shallow impressions in a layer of rock. National Geographic reported that the tracks are preserved in three-dimensional sandstone concretions, allowing the shape of the animal's foot to remain visible even after tens of millions of years. Researchers have found only one other trackway of any kind in the Hell Creek Formation, and it was not attributed to either T. rex or Triceratops.Scientists cannot normally determine a dinosaur's exact species from a footprint alone. Different animals can produce similar three-toed tracks, so researchers considered several lines of evidence when identifying the North Dakota trackmaker. The footprints are exceptionally large, roughly 3 feet long, and have a narrow three-toed shape. The surrounding area also contains abundant T. rex fossils. The researchers therefore identified T. rex as the most likely trackmaker rather than claiming that the footprints alone prove the species. The scientific description says the identification is supported by the tracks' size and morphology together with the abundance of T. rex fossils in the surrounding area.Other fossils found nearby add context. Lyson's team previously recovered a juvenile T. rex nicknamed Teen Rex, located a little more than 10 miles from the trackway. The team also excavated a largely intact Triceratops specimen nicknamed Triceratops Dreams less than half a mile away. A fragment of a tyrannosaur tooth was found on the lower jaw of that Triceratops, although researchers could not determine which tyrannosaur species the tooth came from.The four footprints provide a rare behavioural record. The trackway contains two left and two right prints, with an estimated stride of about 13 feet. Researchers estimate that the animal was moving at roughly 3.5 to 4.5 miles per hour, comparable to a brisk human walking pace. Because the tracks are heavily weathered, the speed estimate remains approximate. High-resolution 3D surface scanning has preserved detailed digital models of the entire trackway, allowing researchers to examine the footprints remotely and create physical reproductions. Three of the fossilised tracks are scheduled to be recovered by helicopter and transported to the Denver Museum of Nature & Science for preparation and further research. Scientists hope the specimens could provide additional information about T. rex foot anatomy, biomechanics and potentially even skin impressions. For Hups, the discovery began with a strange shape in a landscape where he had spent years searching for fossils. What emerged from the rock was not a T. rex skeleton, but a much rarer record of the animal actually walking across the ancient landscape. As Hups put it, a track shows the size of the living foot itself, including the dimensions that bones alone cannot fully convey.
Article Summary: Kent Hups found the first footprint while prospecting for fossils in the Hell Creek Formation of North Dakota. Excavation revealed a sequence of four three- toed footprints stretching about 23 feet across the hillside. Researchers identified an adult Tyrannosaurus rex as the most likely trackmaker, making it the first described trackway likely left by an adult T. rex.

Article Title: In 2003, a Montana family bought 57 acres along the Stillwater River; after cameras documented bears, wolves and mountain lions, they have permanently protected the property from development
Article Text:
A wildlife corridor captured on camera

Nearly a mile of riverfront remains protected

From family land to long-term conservation

A Montana family has permanently protected 57 acres of riverfront land along the Stillwater River after years of documenting the wildlife that moves through the property. The conservation effort was reported by the Flathead Beacon and Whitefish Pilot, while the Flathead Land Trust confirmed details of the newly established conservation easement. Sean and Melodye Rooney purchased the land with Sean’s parents in 2003 and eventually became its sole owners. Located west of Whitefish, the property stretches along nearly a mile of the Stillwater River and is now protected under a conservation easement held by Flathead Land Trust. The agreement permanently prevents subdivision and development while allowing the Rooneys to continue living on and using the property. More than 20 acres remain in hay production, while the rest includes riparian forest, shrubland and wetlands.The property’s conservation value became increasingly clear through the family’s long-term wildlife monitoring. Camera traps placed around the land have recorded an impressive range of species, including grizzly and black bears, mountain lions, gray wolves, moose, river otters and bald eagles. The land is also an official study site for Snapshot USA, a nationwide camera-trapping project that tracks changes in mammal populations across the United States.The project is coordinated nationally by the Smithsonian’s National Zoo and Conservation Biology Institute and its partners. Brigit Rooney, Sean and Melodye’s daughter, serves as Snapshot USA’s survey coordinator. The programme uses standardized camera-trap surveys to study the distribution and long-term trends of mammals in relation to land use, habitat and climate.The Rooneys’ property therefore serves a purpose beyond private conservation, contributing observations to a wider scientific effort. Brigit Rooney is also a co-author of the 2026 Snapshot USA research covering the survey’s sixth year of coordinated national camera-trap data.The conservation easement also safeguards habitat along the Stillwater River, where wetlands and riverfront vegetation play an important role in maintaining the surrounding ecosystem.The property provides habitat for aquatic species including bull trout and westslope cutthroat trout, according to Flathead Land Trust. Its location also connects with two existing conservation easements and nearby U.S. Forest Service and Stillwater State Forest lands, creating a larger network of protected open space. The family has undertaken habitat work as well. In 2025, the Rooneys began a project aimed at restoring a ponded area and associated wetland habitat on the property.The Rooneys’ connection to the Flathead Valley predates their ownership of the Stillwater property. Sean’s grandfather homesteaded near Cut Bank before working for the Great Northern Railway in Whitefish, while his father later settled in the Flathead Valley and taught English and geology at Flathead Valley Community College.The new easement means the 57-acre tract will remain undeveloped even as surrounding areas change. It preserves a combination of wildlife habitat, wetlands, river frontage and working agricultural land, while keeping the property connected to other protected areas along the Stillwater River corridor.For a landscape where wildlife monitoring has revealed bears, wolves and mountain lions using the same trails as people, providing crucial evidence of their continued presence and shared use of this landscape, the conservation agreement turns years of observation into a permanent commitment to keeping the habitat intact.
Article Summary: Montana family has permanently protected 57 acres of riverfront land along the Stillwater River after years of documenting the wildlife that moves through the property. The land is also an official study site for Snapshot USA, a nationwide camera-trapping project that tracks changes in mammal populations across the United States.

Article Title: A conservation group bought nearly 2,000 acres of South Carolina forest before development could reach it; the land has now been transferred to the US government and permanently added to Sumter Nation
Article Text:
Representative image from Canva

A landscape saved just in time

How the deal came together

What the addition means for Sumter National Forest

Why permanent protection matters

A model for future conservation in South Carolina

In a quiet but decisive win for conservation, a 1,950-acre tract of South Carolina forest that once faced the threat of development has been permanently protected as part of Sumter National Forest. The Nature Conservancy purchased the land in 2023, held it while paperwork and funding were finalised, and has now transferred it to the US Forest Service, ensuring the upland hardwoods, wetlands and streams near Joanna in Laurens County remain open to the public for generations. The move, reported by multiple local outlets, adds a significant new block of protected habitat to the Enoree Ranger District and shields the area from the southward creep of development along the I-26 corridor.The newly protected acreage sits in Laurens County, directly adjoining the unincorporated community of Joanna and bordering land that Laurens County is turning into an equestrian park. The property includes large stands of upland hardwood forest, pockets of wetlands and a network of streams that drain into the Enoree River, a tributary of the broader Saluda basin. These habitats support white-tailed deer, wild turkey, songbirds and a range of amphibians and reptiles that depend on intact forest and clean water.Officials with The Nature Conservancy say the purchase was driven by urgency as much as opportunity. As development continues to move south along the I-26 corridor, natural spaces in the Upstate are increasingly under pressure from new housing, commercial projects and infrastructure. The conservancy’s team moved quickly to take the property off the real estate market and managed it until the transfer to the Forest Service could be finalised, preventing the land from being subdivided or sold to private developers.The 1,950-acre transfer traces back to a larger 2,281-acre purchase by The Nature Conservancy in 2023, acquired for about 6.47 million dollars according to local reporting. From that original tract, Laurens County bought a 335-acre parcel in late 2024 with plans to develop an equestrian park that will connect to the Palmetto Trail and Sumter National Forest. The remaining acreage has now been handed over to the US Forest Service to become part of the national forest system.The transaction builds on earlier conservation wins in the same area. In 2025, The Nature Conservancy helped secure the largest conservation easement in Laurens County history at Creekwood Farms, protecting another 2,000-acre tract next to Sumter National Forest through a donated easement valued at 2 million dollars. Together, these deals create a growing mosaic of protected lands that link public forest, county parks and privately held conservation easements into a larger network of open space.Sumter National Forest is already a major public resource in the Upstate, with more than 170,000 acres spread across Newberry, Union, Chester, Laurens and Fairfield counties as part of the Enoree Ranger District. The new 1,950-acre block extends the forest further into Laurens County and strengthens its presence near Joanna, a community that has watched growth inch closer in recent years. Once the US Forest Service formally incorporates the property into the national forest system, it will be opened for public access under the same rules that govern the rest of Sumter.The land will be co-managed for wildlife by the US Forest Service and the South Carolina Department of Natural Resources under the state’s Wildlife Management Area program. That designation keeps the area open for public hunting and fishing, while also supporting hiking, birding and other low-impact recreation. Forest supervisors say they plan to improve public access over time, adding trails and parking areas that connect the new acreage to existing routes in the Enoree Ranger District.Turning the property into part of a national forest does more than keep trees standing. It locks in long-term protections that make it far harder for the land to be sold off, subdivided or converted to other uses. National forest status also brings federal resources for habitat management, invasive species control and trail maintenance, helping ensure the forest remains healthy and accessible.For local residents, the addition offers a tangible buffer against sprawl. As new housing and commercial development push outward from Greenville, Spartanburg and other growing cities, protected forests provide breathing room, cleaner water and places for people to escape into nature without driving for hours. The contiguous block of forest also helps wildlife move across the landscape, reducing the fragmentation that can isolate populations and weaken ecosystems.The Joanna-area deal fits into a broader push to expand protected lands across the state. It supports South Carolina’s Ten Million Acres Initiative, launched by Governor Henry McMaster in 2024, which aims to conserve millions of acres of forests, wetlands and working lands through partnerships with nonprofits, agencies and private landowners. Similar efforts are underway in other parts of the state, including a recent 1,700-acre acquisition along the I-95 corridor that will eventually become a state-owned forest in the Lowcountry.Conservation groups and public agencies say the Sumter expansion shows how strategic purchases, easements and transfers can work together to protect large, connected landscapes before development reaches them. By acting early and holding land until permanent protections are in place, organisations like The Nature Conservancy can give public agencies time to secure funding and complete the legal steps needed to add new areas to national forests and state parks.For now, the most visible result is simple. Nearly 2,000 acres of South Carolina forest that might have become subdivisions or strip malls will instead remain forest, open to the public and permanently part of Sumter National Forest.
Article Summary: The Nature Conservancy purchased the land in 2023, held it while paperwork and funding were finalised, and has now transferred it to the US Forest Service. The move adds a significant new block of protected habitat to the Enoree Ranger District and shields the area from the southward creep of development along the I-26 corridor.

Article Title: Trump to meet Venezuela acting president Delcy Rodriguez, first since Maduro’s removal
Article Text:
The meeting aims to revive the country's battered energy industry with the involvement of American companies.

Who is Delcy Rodriguez?

US President Donald Trump will meet Venezuela’s acting President Delcy Rodriguez in New York on Tuesday, a senior US official said on Friday. This would mark the first in-person meeting between the two leaders since Washington removed former Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro in January.The meeting will take place on the sidelines of a reception hosted by Trump for leaders attending the UN General Assembly, US ambassador to the UN Mike Waltz said during a briefing call. The talks are expected to bring Trump and Rodriguez together as Washington continues to engage with Venezuela over its energy sector."The president will host a UN General Assembly leaders' reception. There, he'll participate in a pull-aside with the acting president Rodriguez of Venezuela," Waltz said.Waltz did not provide details on what the two leaders would discuss. Venezuela's communications ministry, which handles press queries for the government, did not immediately respond to a request for comment.The meeting comes weeks after the US and Venezuela signed an energy agreement that would allow Washington to take partial control of Venezuela's vast oil reserves. The deal aims to revive the country's battered energy industry with the involvement of American companies.The development also comes as Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado faces uncertainty over when to return to the country and seek public support. Machado left Venezuela late last year to receive the Nobel Peace Prize after largely living in hiding following the disputed 2024 election.Machado had sought to build an alliance with Trump well before Maduro's removal. Since Maduro was ousted, however, Trump has repeatedly expressed support for Rodriguez.Rodriguez, Maduro's former deputy, became Venezuela's acting president after Washington removed Maduro in January. Her rise to power has since brought her government into direct engagement with the Trump administration, including the recent energy agreement.
Article Summary: The meeting will take place on the sidelines of a reception hosted by Trump for leaders attending the UN General Assembly. The talks are expected to bring Trump and Rodriguez together as Washington continues to engage with Venezuela over its energy sector. The deal aims to revive the country's battered energy industry with the involvement of American companies.

Article Title: Iran war costs US $45.1 billion; fatalities possibly higher than 18 reported by Pentagon
Article Text:
File photo: Shredded tents, destroyed jet: Images reveal hidden scale of Iranian strikes on US Gulf bases

Human toll also under scrutiny

War’s wider costs

The human and material cost of America’s war with Iran is proving larger than previously disclosed, with the Pentagon telling Congress that the conflict has cost $45.1 billion so far, while a Washington Post report said the number of US military fatalities may also be higher than the Pentagon’s publicly reported tally.The Pentagon told lawmakers that the war had cost $43.6 billion as of September 3, with another $1.5 billion spent on additional fuel, according to CNN, citing sources familiar with the matter. The estimate does not include the cost of repairing damaged US military bases and buildings or provide a full accounting of indirect operational costs.The latest figure is higher than the Congressional Budget Office’s estimate of $38 billion through August 1. The CBO has estimated that the war could cost the US another $2 billion to $3 billion a month for as long as fighting continues.Separately, six US officials familiar with the Pentagon’s internal casualty accounting told the Washington Post that at least 22 US service members had died in the Middle East since the war began, four more than the 18 fatalities listed in the Pentagon’s public casualty database as of Friday.One official put the number at 23, saying not all of the additional deaths were directly tied to combat but involved US personnel in the region amid the ongoing hostilities. Three US contractors based in the region have also died since combat operations began, according to the report.The Pentagon declined to address questions about the discrepancy, while details surrounding the additional deaths, including the identities of those killed and when, how and where they died, remained unclear.The financial estimate also does not capture the full cost of damage to US military infrastructure. US Central Command estimated the war had cost $43.6 billion through early September, including $28 billion to replace munitions and more than $4.3 billion in lost or damaged equipment.The conflict has also put pressure on US weapons stocks and disrupted global energy markets after Iran closed the Strait of Hormuz and Houthis have control of the Bab al-Mandeb Strait. The CBO said the war could push inflation 0.5 percentage points higher in the first quarter of 2027 because of higher energy prices.
Article Summary: Pentagon tells Congress that the conflict has cost $45.1 billion so far. Congressional Budget Office estimates that the war could cost the US another $2 billion to $3 billion a month for as long as fighting continues. Washington Post report says number of US military fatalities may also be higher than the Pentagon’s publicly reported tally.

Article Title: 'Almost started a war': How an AI error led to a close call between US and China
Article Text:
The chatbot used by a US Special Operations Command analyst had incorrectly identified the material listed in the ship's manifest

AI error reaches military chain

From battlefield intelligence to weapons

An intelligence report circulated across the US military this spring during the war with Iran set off an alarming chain of events after it claimed that a Chinese ship in the Middle East was carrying components linked to a nuclear weapons programme.According to CNN, the report prompted the US military to prepare an operation to intercept the vessel. Armed US personnel were preparing to board the ship, while military aircraft were already in the air, according to sources familiar with the episode. It was only shortly before the planned operation that officials took a closer look at the intelligence and discovered that it had been produced with the assistance of artificial intelligence.The chatbot used by a US Special Operations Command analyst had incorrectly identified the material listed in the ship's manifest. The resulting intelligence report, described by one source as "entirely false", had travelled through official channels and was being treated as credible military intelligence. "It almost started a war," the source told CNN.The incident began when the analyst examined intelligence about the ship's manifest that originated with US Special Operations Command Pacific, based in Hawaii.The analyst queried a chatbot about the information, but the AI system incorrectly identified the cargo.The chatbot had combined open-source information with classified signals intelligence held by the US government before reaching its conclusion. The analyst then used AI again to turn the findings into a standard intelligence report, giving the information the format and appearance of conventional military intelligence before it was disseminated.CNN reported that it could not establish whether the chatbot was a commercially available system or an AI tool developed for the US government. A former senior US official familiar with the systems used by military and intelligence analysts told CNN that internal tools were "mostly just copies of the commercial stuff wearing lipstick".The episode highlights the risks of relying on AI-generated analysis in situations where decisions have to be made rapidly and the consequences of an error can extend beyond the battlefield. Any US attempt to board or otherwise confront a Chinese vessel could have risked escalating into a broader confrontation between Washington and Beijing.US military and intelligence agencies are nevertheless rapidly expanding their use of AI. The technology is being explored for analysing huge volumes of intelligence, selecting targets, moving military assets and handling logistics, budgeting and supply chains. Defence officials have argued that faster AI-assisted decision-making could be critical in a future conflict with China or another major adversary.In January, US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth released the Pentagon's "Artificial Intelligence Acceleration Strategy", aimed at speeding up the military's adoption of AI.The episode comes as governments, militaries and AI companies grapple with another question: how increasingly capable AI systems can be prevented from being misused for military purposes.Anthropic recently reported that a Yemen-based weapons engineering cell had used its Claude AI model to develop guidance, navigation and control software for missiles and a guided rocket. The company said the group used Claude Code in place of human software engineers to integrate an open-source autopilot with a phone-class flight computer, write control software, tune settings, run firmware builds and conduct flight simulations.Anthropic said there was no evidence that the group successfully deployed an operational weapon, although it carried out a test launch of a guided rocket that appeared to fail. The company said safeguards blocked many requests but not all, while the group repeatedly tried to circumvent restrictions.The Yemen case was among several conventional-weapons operations identified by Anthropic, including work involving drone swarms, torpedo interception and targeting systems for electronic warfare and air-defence suppression. The company also identified around 35 potentially concerning biological research efforts over a 30-day period, while cautioning that it could not determine whether those activities were intended for harm or legitimate scientific research.The concerns are now extending to the highest levels of international security discussions. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman is due to brief the UN Security Council on AI and international security next week, according to Reuters. The meeting comes as governments consider how increasingly powerful AI systems should be governed and how common safety standards could be established.
Article Summary: Report claimed Chinese ship was carrying components linked to nuclear weapons. Report prompted the US military to prepare an operation to intercept the vessel. It was only shortly before the planned operation that officials took a closer look at the intelligence. The report had been produced with the assistance of artificial intelligence.

Article Title: US clears $2.7 billion Ukraine arms package to bolster air defences
Article Text:
The announcement came as Russian forces continued attacks across Ukraine

The US State Department has approved a possible $2.68 billion military sale to Ukraine for air-defence development upgrades, equipment and related services, as Kyiv faces continued Russian attacks and seeks stronger security support from its allies.The department announced the determination late on Friday, describing the package as focused on upgrading Ukraine’s air-defence capabilities. The proposed sale comes as US-mediated efforts to end Russia’s more than four-year full-scale invasion have stalled, with territorial concessions in eastern Ukraine remaining a key sticking point in negotiations.Ukraine has also been seeking security guarantees from its partners as part of any potential settlement.The announcement came as Russian forces continued attacks across Ukraine. Two people were killed and two others injured in overnight strikes in the Zhytomyr region, according to Ukraine’s State Emergency Service. The strikes triggered fires at warehouse and production buildings, while repeated air raid alerts disrupted rescue operations.In the Kharkiv region, one person was killed and six injured after a Russian drone struck an electric train at a railway station in the Novovodolazka community.The attack set two carriages on fire. Another Russian drone attack destroyed a shopping complex in Zaporizhzhia and injured one person.Russia’s Defence Ministry also said its forces struck Ukrainian ports, vessels and a military logistics centre. It said a bulk carrier was hit at the port of Chornomorsk and that a Nova Poshta logistics facility near Odesa, allegedly used to store and distribute military cargo from Europe, was targeted.The ministry separately said Russian air defences intercepted and destroyed 629 Ukrainian drones overnight across 14 Russian regions, Crimea and areas around the Azov and Black seas. Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said more than 350 drones were headed towards the Russian capital, with 64 reportedly downed as they approached the city.The US arms approval also comes as Ukraine receives additional European financial support. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Kyiv had received a 3.3 billion-euro tranche, worth roughly $3.8 billion, from an EU support package intended to strengthen defence capabilities, including through the purchase of missiles and drones.Zelenskyy made the remarks as Ukraine hosted the inaugural “Carpathian Eight” summit in western Ukraine, bringing together regional leaders to discuss security, energy, logistics and economic cooperation.
Article Summary: The proposed sale comes as US-mediated efforts to end Russia’s more than four- year full-scale invasion have stalled. Ukraine has also been seeking security guarantees from its partners as part of any potential settlement. Two people were killed and two others injured in overnight strikes in the Zhytomyr region.

Article Title: NYT alleges MS, OpenAI knew using its news content was theft
Article Text:
NYT sued OpenAI and MS three years ago

OpenAI committed "an astonishing theft of unprecedented proportions" when it used millions of news articles to train its AI models, the NYT alleged in a court document unsealed Thursday. The AI lab scraped content from over 10 million articles, nearly a third of which came from the NYT alone.The document claims Microsoft's director of applied science Brent Hect called it "an astonishing theft of unprecedented proportions" and possibly the "largest theft of labour in human history." Hect also allegedly warned that OpenAI might have engaged in an "accidental cover up" in its attempts to identify content in its systems that came from the NYT and the lawsuit's other plaintiffs.NYT sued OpenAI and MS three years ago for allegedly stealing its copyrighted material to train OpenAI's ChatGPT. Several other news publishers also joined the lawsuit. They are seeking damages for each article allegedly stolen and used by OpenAI's models.(This is an AFP story)
Article Summary: NYT sued OpenAI and MS three years ago for allegedly stealing its copyrighted material to train OpenAI's ChatGPT. The AI lab scraped content from over 10 million articles, nearly a third of which came from the NYT alone.

Article Title: Anthropic quietly sets up biology lab for AI drug project
Article Text:
The Dario Amodei-led startup has said it wants to unlock treatments for rare diseases

SAN FRANCISCO: Anthropic has set up a wet lab in San Francisco Bay Area, expanding its artificial intelligence ambitions into physical biology and drug science, according to two people familiar with the matter and company life sciences head Eric Kauderer-Abrams.The Dario Amodei-led startup has said it wants to unlock treatments for rare diseases, taking its biology work beyond computer evaluations. A spokesperson said the lab was not specifically for drug discovery but declined to elaborate. "We believe that to do biology, the final test is still and will be for a while in real lab work," Kauderer-Abrams said. He said Anthropic conducted some work in its facilities and some with external partners.Anthropic wants its Claude AI to direct robotic units conducting experiments with limited human intervention, a source said. Its spokesperson said human involvement remained essential for safety."In our life-science work, we're always balancing these things," Kauderer-Abrams said, "making models better in ways that we think will uplift and accelerate developing medicines, and being thoughtful about how we deploy it to limit the risk."Anthropic said in June it planned preclinical work in areas traditional companies found financially unattractive. It launched Claude Science, added Novartis CEO Vas Narasimhan to its board and acquired Coefficient Bio for about $400 million in stock, according to media reports. Anthropic confirmed the acquisition but not the price.The company is expanding in-house laboratory work for speed and firsthand biology experience, while outsourcing where efficient. Job advertisements indicate it is hiring for procurement and operations as well as protein and nucleic acid characterisation. Life sciences is already among its biggest investment areas by staff.Anthropic believes AI could accelerate work on previously "undruggable" conditions, including development of complex antibodies. However, the diseases targeted and its progress remain unclear. It is not conducting clinical trials for now, focusing on needs industry would not address. Reuters
Article Summary: Anthropic has set up a wet lab in San Francisco Bay Area, expanding its artificial intelligence ambitions. The Dario Amodei-led startup has said it wants to unlock treatments for rare diseases. The company is expanding in-house laboratory work for speed and firsthand biology experience, while outsourcing where efficient.

Article Title: 'Can't afford petrol': Pakistan PTI lawmakers ride donkey carts to assembly in protest
Article Text:
(Image credit: Dawn) “The ministers and (treasury) MPAs should also reach the assembly the same way on donkey carts,” PTI MPA Sajjad Ali was seen saying in a video while holding a placard describing the fuel price hike as a “petrol bomb dropped on the people”.

Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) workers and provincial lawmakers staged a protest in the Sindh province against soaring fuel prices. They arrived at the provincial assembly by riding donkey carts, saying petrol had become too expensive for them to travel in their vehicles.According to Dawn news, the protest was held after petrol prices rose to Rs 390.79 per litre and high-speed diesel (HSD) to Rs 424.92 per litre following the latest adjustment on Thursday. PTI MPA Sajjad Ali and other lawmakers rode donkey carts from areas near the assembly to its main gate, carrying placards and raising slogans against the federal government.“The ministers and (treasury) MPAs should also reach the assembly the same way on donkey carts,” Ali was seen saying in a video while holding a placard describing the fuel price hike as a “petrol bomb dropped on the people”.Ali said the protest was intended to highlight the difficulties faced by ordinary people because of rising fuel costs.“Petrol has become so expensive that we cannot even come to the assembly in our vehicles,” he said, adding that people were bearing the brunt of the government’s policies.The latest increase comes amid renewed hostilities in the Middle East, which have disrupted major oil supply routes and pushed fuel prices higher over the past two months.The current petrol and diesel prices include government taxes and duties of Rs114 per litre on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel. The government now adjusts fuel prices daily.The Pakistan bar council also criticised the repeated fuel price increases. A joint meeting of its Executive Committee and Rules Committee on Thursday called the hikes unprecedented and urged the government to take steps to control prices and provide relief to citizens.The government has meanwhile introduced a relief scheme targeting users of motorcycles, rickshaws, Qingqis and other two- and three-wheelers, as well as small cars with engines up to 800cc.Under the scheme, motorcycle, rickshaw and other eligible two- and three-wheeler users can receive relief on 20 litres of petrol a month. Owners of cars with engines up to 800cc are eligible for a Rs 100-per-litre relief on 30 litres of petrol each month.However, the scheme faced problems on its first day of nationwide rollout on Thursday, with several petrol pumps refusing to accept the digital app introduced for the subsidy. The pumps said they lacked the required system to sell petrol at Rs100 per litre less.The federal government also brought back austerity measures on Thursday. These include ordering markets to close by 9pm and cutting fuel allocations for official vehicles by 50% for three months.
Article Summary: Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) workers and provincial lawmakers staged a protest in the Sindh province against soaring fuel prices. They arrived at the provincial assembly by riding donkey carts, saying petrol had become too expensive for them to travel in their vehicles. “The ministers and (treasury) MPAs should also reach the assembly the same way,” PTI MPA Sajjad Ali was seen saying.

Article Title: 21 security personnel dead in blast at police line in Pakistan
Article Text:
The blast was reported near the Old Police Lines in Kohat, in northwestern Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province.

Around 21 Pakistani security personnel were killed and dozens more injured in a suicide bombing during Friday prayers at the police lines in Kohat, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Some civilians deaths are feared but their exact number could not be ascertained. The facility was struck post noon with a vehicle-borne improvised explosive device, enabling multiple attackers to force their way inside the premises, shooting indiscriminately.An SP-rank officer, a deputy SP and three inspectors of the CTD were among those killed, sources said. Around 80 individuals, mostly police personnel, were admitted to hospitals for treatment. The toll is likely to rise as many of the injured were reported to be critical.No group officially claimed the attack till late Friday though the role of Ittehad-ul-Mujahideen Pakistan (IMP), an umbrella militant alliance formed by three armed groups operating in the region, is alleged. Another group named Inqilabi Islami Pakistan, affiliated to al-Qaida in the Indian subcontinent, also claimed the attack on Telegram.The explosion occurred near a mosque in the facility, reducing the building to rubble and prompting a major rescue and clearing operation. Three to five gunmen besides the driver of the car laden with explosives are suspected to have participated in the attack and were seen attempting to enter the police compound while exchanging fire. The car exploded after ramming into the mosque's entrance wall. Videos uploaded by locals on social media showed the extent of the damage and people frantically running for cover amid dense smoke.Pro-IMP accounts on Telegram claimed the attack, saying their Al Badr suicide brigade had carried out an 'Ishtashadi operation' at the counter-terrorism division premises.
Article Summary: The blast occurred near the Old Police Lines in Kohat, in northwestern Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province. An SP-rank officer, a deputy SP and three inspectors of the CTD were among those killed, sources said. Around 80 individuals, mostly police personnel, were admitted to hospitals for treatment.

Article Title: BLA claims 43 Pakistani personnel, ‘death squad’ members killed in Balochistan
Article Text:
Balochistan sees fresh wave of violence as BLA claims 43 killed in 13 operations

The Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) has claimed that 43 Pakistani military personnel and members of alleged state-backed 'death squads' were killed in 13 operations across Balochistan between September 7 and 13, according to a report.The Balochistan Post (TBP) said that in its weekly statement, BLA spokesperson Jeeyand Baloch said the group’s militants carried out attacks and blockades across areas including Basima, Kharan, Panjgur, Chagai, Tump, Surab, Killa Abdullah, Lasbela, Jiwani and Mashkel.The development comes as a powerful blast at a mosque inside a police compound in Kohat, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, killed at least 16 people and injured 57, police and rescue officials said on Friday. Five police officers and 11 civilians were among the dead. Seven armed gunmen also tried to enter the compound, with six killed in the ensuing gunfire.According to the BLA statement, the operations targeted military convoys, checkpoints and surveillance equipment, alongside people the BLA described as members of “death squads”. The group also reported attacks on commercial vehicles, bridges and a lithium extraction project.The claims could not be independently verified.The campaign allegedly began on September 7 with a five-hour blockade of a China-Pakistan Economic Corridor route in Basima, where the BLA said its fighters conducted checks. It claimed five Pakistani personnel were killed and several injured, while three BLA militants also died in the clashes.The following day, the group claimed an ambush on a military convoy in Kharan left at least four personnel killed or wounded. In Panjgur, it said militants attacked military supply vehicles and destroyed surveillance cameras.On September 10, the BLA claimed it blocked the Quetta-Taftan trade route in Chagai, seized two commercial vehicles and destroyed a bridge with explosives. It also claimed one of its units brought down a Pakistani military surveillance quadcopter in Tump.Two attacks were reported in Surab on September 11. The BLA claimed six military personnel were killed in an ambush on a convoy at Tobo, while another three were killed and four injured during a separate clash at Rodeni Cross.In Lasbela on September 12, the group claimed an attack on a military bomb-disposal convoy destroyed two vehicles and damaged two others, killing nine personnel and injuring more than 11.The BLA also claimed that 25 members of an alleged 'death squad' were killed in Killa Abdullah on September 13, followed by a four-hour clash involving Pakistani forces and the militants. Five BLA fighters were also reported killed.The group said 10 of its BLA militants were killed during the operations and vowed that its “military confrontation will continue on every front”, until Pakistani forces withdraw and an independent Balochistan is established.
Article Summary: Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) claims 43 Pakistani military personnel and members of alleged state-backed 'death squads' were killed in 13 operations between September 7 and 13. BLA spokesperson Jeeyand Baloch said the group’s militants carried out attacks and blockades across areas including Basima, Kharan, Panjgur, Chagai, Tump, Surab and Killa Abdullah.

Article Title: Pakistan suicide blast: Mosque destroyed, people rescue survivors from under rubble - videos
Article Text:
At least 16 killed and dozens injured in a suicide blast at a mosque

At least 16 people, including five police personnel, were killed and dozens injured in a suicide blast at a mosque during Friday prayers at the Kohat Police Lines in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province of northwest Pakistan, as reported by the Dawn.Videos showed extensive destruction at the mosque near the old Police Lines, around 60 kilometres southwest of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa's capital Peshawar, following the explosion.Social media footage showed the mosque’s roof had collapsed, with rescuers and residents pulling injured people from the rubble and carrying them to ambulances.No group or individual has so far claimed responsibility for the attack.Citing District Headquarters Hospital Medical Superintendent Tahir Ali Shah, Geo News reported that 15 bodies were brought to the hospital along with more than 50 injured following the blast.Police said most of those injured were worshippers, adding that the explosion caused a crater outside the mosque.Rescue 1122 Khyber Pakhtunkhwa spokesperson Bilal Ahmad Faizi said rescue teams reached the site shortly after receiving information about the blast and launched a rescue operation, as cited by PTI.He said several of the injured were shifted to nearby hospitals for initial medical treatment.Faizi said rescue teams remained at the scene and were assessing the situation.
Article Summary: At least 16 people, including five police personnel, killed and dozens injured in a suicide blast at a mosque in northwest Pakistan. The blast occurred during Friday prayers at the Kohat Police Lines in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province. No group or individual has yet claimed responsibility for the attack.

Article Title: Explosive-laden truck rams into mosque near police offices in Pakistan's Kohat; 21 dead
Article Text:
A blast was reported near the Old Police Lines in Kohat, in Pakistan’s northwestern Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province.

At least 21 people were killed and more than 80 injured in a suicide explosion at a mosque inside the Kohat Police Lines in Pakistan's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province on Friday, officials said.The explosion occured in Kohat, a district in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, near the Afghanistan border, during Friday prayers, bringing down part of the building and prompting a major rescue operation. Emergency responders and local residents searched through the rubble for survivors, while at least two armed gunmen attempted to storm the police compound and were killed in an exchange of fire with officers. Around three others reportedly moved towards the Special Branch building.According to Dawn, Rescue 1122 Khyber Pakhtunkhwa spokesperson Bilal Ahmed Faizi said emergency teams rushed to the site after receiving information about the explosion and began rescue operations.The injured were taken to nearby hospitals for treatment, while roads leading to the blast site were closed, Geo News reported. Rescue teams remained at the scene to assess the situation.The location was initially described by rescue officials as being near the Old Police Lines.However, a statement from Khyber Pakhtunkhwa inspector general Zulfiqar Hameed said the explosion occurred at a mosque inside the Police Lines complex.“Following the explosion, an exchange of fire ensued with the armed terrorists,” the statement said. Hameed also directed officials to ensure the best possible medical treatment for those injured in the blast.Separately, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa chief minister Sohail Afridi and governor Faisal Karim Kundi condemned the explosion and expressed solidarity with those affected. The blast comes a day after a roadside bomb targeted a security forces convoy in northwestern Hangu district, killing six soldiers. Additionally government forces carried out raids in several areas on Thursday and killed 10 militants suspected to be affiliated with the Pakistani Taliban.Footage circulating on social media showed the roof of the mosque had collapsed. Rescuers and local residents could be seen pulling injured people from the rubble and carrying them to ambulances.The attack was claimed by a seperatist group led by Hafiz Gul Bahadur. Suspicion could nevertheless fall on the Pakistani Taliban, or Tehrik-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), which has carried out repeated attacks against security personnel and civilians in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, AP said.In 2023, a suicide bombing at a mosque in Peshawar, the provincial capital, killed 101 people. The TTP is separate from Afghanistan's Taliban but maintains an alliance with the group.Pakistan has repeatedly accused the Taliban government in Kabul of providing shelter to TTP members and allowing cross-border attacks to be carried out from Afghan territory. Kabul has denied the allegations.Authorities have yet to establish the precise nature of Friday's explosion or identify those responsible. Further details are expected as investigators assess the scene and the condition of those injured.
Article Summary: At least 21 people were killed and more than 80 injured in a suicide explosion at a mosque inside the Kohat Police Lines in Pakistan's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province. The explosion occured during Friday prayers, bringing down part of the building and prompting a major rescue operation. At least two armed gunmen attempted to storm the police compound and were killed in an exchange of fire with officers.

Article Title: No official dinners, foreign travel: Pakistan rolls out austerity measures amid fuel shock
Article Text:
Fuel shock hits Pakistan

Pakistan on Thursday announced a fresh set of austerity measures, including a 50 per cent cut in fuel allocations for government vehicles and a ban on official foreign travel and the purchase of new government vehicles. The measures come as rising global oil prices threaten fuel, gas and power supplies.The measures, approved by the Pakistan cabinet, will remain in force for three months as the government seeks to reduce fuel consumption and public expenditure.Under the new restrictions, markets will have to close by 9 pm, while marriage halls can operate until 10 pm and restaurants until 11 pm. Drug stores and medical laboratories have been exempted.Fuel allocations for government vehicles will be reduced by half, although vehicles used by the armed forces, law enforcement agencies and essential services will not be covered by the cut.The Shehbaz Sharif government has also ordered a five per cent reduction in non-employee-related expenditure and prohibited official foreign visits and domestic travel for meetings, directing officials to use virtual meetings instead.Official dinners have been banned, except those hosted for foreign visitors and delegations. The purchase of new government vehicles has also been prohibited, while procurement of durable goods has been restricted, with IT purchases exempted.The measures come two days after Pakistan raised petrol prices by PkR 4.10 per litre and high-speed diesel (HSD) by PkR 6.41 per litre. Petrol now costs PkR 384.34 per litre, while HSD is priced at PkR 415.83.Global oil prices have risen amid continuing conflict and supply concerns in West Asia, including attacks on energy infrastructure in Saudi Arabia and the temporary closure of its East-West oil pipeline following an aerial attack.The austerity package is the second such effort this year. Pakistan introduced similar measures in March, including a temporary school shutdown, reductions in government fuel use and greater reliance on remote working.Earlier the government had introduced the Prime Minister's Fuel Relief Scheme from Wednesday, offering motorcycle, rickshaw and small-car owners a subsidy of 100 rupees (36 US cents) per litre on a capped monthly quota.The programme, however, has faced implementation difficulties. Karachi resident Mohammad Musharraf told Reuters: "First of all, you have to register your vehicle. Then you have to register your mobile phone. How can an illiterate person survive if the conditions are so difficult?"The energy pressures extend beyond transport. Reuters reported that Pakistan's power sector could require up to 400 million cubic feet of gas a day through winter, while only two LNG cargoes had been confirmed for September.
Article Summary: Pakistan announces new austerity measures, including a 50 per cent cut in fuel allocations for government vehicles and a ban on official foreign travel. The measures come as rising global oil prices threaten fuel, gas and power supplies. Pakistan raised petrol prices by PkR 4.10 per litre and high-speed diesel by PKR 6.41 per litres.

Article Title: ‘Absolutely no ambiguity: Pakistan says Mecca pact applies as Saudi Arabia faces Houthi drone threat
Article Text:
File photo: Pakistan defence minister Khwaja Asif

Pakistan keeps military response details confidential

Saudi Arabia faces Houthi drone and missile threat

Islamabad urges diplomacy, warns over Red Sea

Poll Vote & Share your view What is your stance on the recent statements from Pakistan indicating military confidentiality? It's wise for national security It raises concerns about accountability 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Pakistan on Thursday said it was committed to implementing its defence agreement with Saudi Arabia and Turkiye amid escalating tensions in the Gulf region following what Riyadh described as an attempted Houthi drone attack near the Muslim holy city of Mecca.The trilateral Mecca defence agreement, signed by Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye last month, establishes a framework for collective deterrence and stipulates that an armed attack against any one of the three countries would be regarded as an attack against all.Pakistan defence minister Khawaja Asif said Islamabad was fully prepared to fulfil its obligations under the pact.“The Mecca Agreement applies to us, and we will fulfil our duty,” Asif was quoted as saying by Geo News.Also read| Mecca Pact, but no troops yet: Pakistan expresses 'solidarity' with Saudi Arabia after Houthi attacks on kingdom Asif’s comments came after Saudi authorities said their air defences had intercepted and destroyed a Houthi drone south of Mecca. The drone was destroyed before entering the city’s prohibited airspace, according to Saudi authorities.The Houthis denied targeting Mecca or any Islamic holy site.“If Mecca is attacked, there is no need for an agreement to protect it,” Asif was quoted as saying.He said Pakistan did not need a formal agreement to protect the Muslim holy sites and that safeguarding them was a duty even without the pact.During his weekly briefing on Thursday, Pakistan foreign office spokesperson Sajjad Haider Khan reiterated Islamabad’s commitment to implementing the agreement.Asked whether any mechanism had been devised for Pakistan to help thwart recent Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia, Khan said Pakistan remained committed to “implementing” the agreement.“However, when, how, where and what force will be used against what objectives, in which modes and matters — operational confidentiality requires us to be discreet at this stage,” he said.Asif had also said on Wednesday that there was “absolutely no ambiguity” about the pact’s application if the territorial integrity or geographical boundaries of any of the three countries were violated.He stressed, however, that Pakistan would not publicly discuss its defence or military strategy.The latest tensions follow Saudi Arabia’s accusation that the Houthis attempted to target Mecca with a drone. The group denied the allegation.The attacks have also put the newly signed defence pact under scrutiny. Pakistan’s military has described the agreement as defensive and intended for collective deterrence, with “no regional aspirations”.Pakistan’s Inter-Services public relations chief Lt Gen Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry said the operational details of the pact were classified and would be decided by the three countries if the agreement were triggered.Also read| Pak scrambles to define Mecca pact after Houthi attack The pact was signed on August 7 and states that an armed attack against any one of the three members would be regarded as an attack against all.Saudi Arabia had sought air-defence support from France, Britain, Pakistan and Egypt as it faced shortages of missile interceptors. However, officials from Pakistan and Turkiye told news agency AP that they had not received a Saudi request for military support in response to the latest Houthi escalation.Pakistan’s foreign office also highlighted the wider security risks from the conflict.Khan described the situation around Bab el-Mandeb as “exceptionally serious” and called on the Houthis to stop their activities.He said Pakistan had long advocated peace and stability in the region because “this is not only in the interest of Pakistan and Iran, but also the entire region and beyond.”“In this regard, our discussions basically revolve around bringing peace and stability through dialogue and diplomacy and not through coercive measures,” Khan said.Asif said Pakistan had conveyed Saudi Arabia’s message to Iran amid concerns over Houthi attacks against the kingdom.He said he did not think Iran as a state would open another front, while distinguishing between the Iranian government and non-state groups that could act without formal approval from a state.He said Pakistan would continue efforts to prevent the conflict from expanding into additional theatres.The defence minister also said disruptions to maritime routes, including the Strait of Hormuz and Bab el-Mandab, were affecting trade and economies across the region. He said the disruption was particularly important for Pakistan because of its impact on the country’s economy.Turkey’s defence ministry condemned the Houthi drone attack targeting Saudi Arabia and other actions by the group.The ministry said the continued Houthi threat in the Red Sea and Bab el-Mandab was negatively affecting regional security, international maritime trade and global stability.Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Wednesday reiterated Pakistan’s full support for Saudi Arabia’s defence and said Islamabad stood “shoulder to shoulder” with Riyadh.Sharif condemned what he described as a “dastardly and heinous attempted drone attack” against the holy city and urged all parties to exercise maximum restraint and avoid further escalation.
Article Summary: Pakistan committed to implementing its defence agreement with Saudi Arabia and Turkiye. Defence minister Khawaja Asif said Islamabad was fully prepared to fulfil its obligations under the pact. Pakistan’s military has described the agreement as defensive and intended for collective deterrence, with “no regional aspirations”

Article Title: BLA claims killing 43 Pakistan military personnel past week
Article Text:
BLA said it imposed multi-hour blockades on Besima-Kapuk and Quetta-Taftan trade routes

Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) has claimed responsibility for 13 coordinated attacks across Balochistan over the past week, saying its fighters killed 43 Pakistani military and state-affiliated "Death Squad" personnel. The rebel group acknowledged losing 10 fighters.BLA spokesperson Jeeyand Baloch said the operations, involving road blockades, targeted strikes, took place in Besima, Kharan, Panjgur, Chagai, Surab, Qila Abdullah and Awaran, where it claimed two Pakistani army soldiers were killed.According to the statement, BLA said it imposed multi-hour blockades on Besima-Kapuk and Quetta-Taftan trade routes to conduct snap checks and restrict troop movements. It claimed 25 personnel were killed on Sept 13 in an ambush on state-aligned local militias in Sultan Charak, Qila Abdullah, followed by a four-hour clash with army reinforcements.The group also claimed its "Fateh Squad" killed nine soldiers in Lasbela, while another operation targeted four military intelligence operatives in Jiwani. It said fighters destroyed surveillance equipment in Panjgur and burnt machinery at a lithium extraction site in Machil under its "economic blockade". BLA said it would continue armed resistance until Pakistani security forces withdrew from the region entirely. On Monday, it released a video purportedly showing fighters seizing 14 posts on Quetta-Taftan Highway.
Article Summary: Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) claims responsibility for 13 coordinated attacks across Balochistan over the past week. It says its fighters killed 43 Pakistani military and state-affiliated "Death Squad" personnel. BLA said it would continue armed resistance until Pakistani security forces withdrew from the region entirely.

Article Title: 'It is defensive, nothing aggressive': Pak scrambles to define Mecca pact after Houthi attack
Article Text:
File photo: Pakistan's military spokesperson Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry

What happens if Saudi Arabia is attacked?

Not a Muslim military bloc

Pakistan says pact does not compete with China ties

Why Pakistan is walking a diplomatic tightrope

Pakistan’s military has rushed to give a definition to the newly formed Mecca Defence Alliance, saying the pact with Saudi Arabia and Turkey is meant for collective deterrence and has “no regional aspirations”, even as questions grow over how the agreement would work if one of its members comes under attack.Pakistan’s inter-services public relations (ISPR) director general Lt Gen Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry, speaking to Al Arabiya, said the agreement was “defensive” and “complementary” to the three countries’ existing alliances and relationships.“It is defensive. There’s nothing aggressive. There are no regional aspirations. It is collective deterrence,” Chaudhry said.The comments come as the pact faces questions over its first potential test. The alliance has been put under scrutiny amid the conflict involving Saudi Arabia and Houthi forces, with uncertainty over whether Riyadh has sought military assistance from Islamabad and how Pakistan would respond if it did.The pact was signed on August 7 and says an attack on one member would be treated as an attack on all. Pakistan is to initially head its secretariat for three years.Also read: Mecca Pact, but no troops yet: Pakistan expresses 'solidarity' with Saudi Arabia after Houthi attacks on kingdom Chaudhry was pressed on precisely that question during the Al Arabiya interview: whether Pakistan had a mutual defence obligation under the agreement and what it would actually do if one of the members came under attack.He said the publicly released text made the mutual defence commitment clear, but stressed that the operational details of how such a commitment would be implemented were classified.“What you’re asking is the how part — how we are going to defend Pakistan against any aggression,” he said, adding that such decisions would be for the three countries to make.The distinction is significant because the pact has not yet been tested in an actual conflict. The first major test could become the escalating Houthi-Saudi confrontation, with questions remaining over when an attack would trigger the alliance and what form military assistance would take.The uncertainty is also not entirely new. Pakistan’s parliament had unanimously rejected a request in 2015 to send troops to join the Saudi-led coalition against the Houthis. Pakistan also shares a long border with Iran, giving Islamabad an additional security consideration as it navigates its relationship with Riyadh and Tehran.Chaudhry also rejected the idea that the Mecca Defence Alliance was being designed as a broader Muslim military bloc.“There is nothing in the pact that says that it is a Muslim alliance,” he said, describing it instead as an arrangement aimed at regional stability.He said other countries could potentially join if they shared the principles of non-aggression, non-interference and collective deterrence, but stressed that any expansion would be a decision for the leaders of Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkey.The comments come amid speculation about possible expansion of the grouping. Turkey had previously suggested Egypt could join, although Cairo has not confirmed any such move. Pakistan’s foreign office has meanwhile said the immediate priority was to consolidate the new organisation before considering expansion.Chaudhry also sought to reassure Beijing that the new arrangement was not aimed at competing with Pakistan’s relationship with China.Asked whether the alliance complemented or competed with Islamabad’s ties with Beijing, he said it was complementary.He argued that Pakistan’s relationships with Saudi Arabia and Turkey were longstanding and that the three countries also maintained good relations with China.“Everyone understands that this is defensive,” Chaudhry said, adding that the pact was intended to maintain “stability and peace in the region”.The military spokesperson was also asked whether the defence pact complicated Pakistan’s efforts to mediate between the US and Iran amid the ongoing Middle East conflict.Chaudhry rejected that suggestion, saying the pact formalised longstanding relationships rather than creating a new strategic alignment against another country.He described Pakistan as being in a “unique position” because of its engagement with different countries and said Islamabad could therefore act as an “objective arbiter of peace” and an “honest broker”.Pakistan, he said, wanted a negotiated and peaceful resolution rather than a military solution.That position is particularly relevant as Islamabad balances its strategic relationship with Saudi Arabia with its geographic proximity to Iran.Chaudhry said Pakistan's decision to mediate was driven by a desire for regional peace and that the country would continue engaging the parties involved.
Article Summary: Pakistan's military has given a definition to the newly formed Mecca Defence Alliance. The pact with Saudi Arabia and Turkey is meant for collective deterrence. Pakistan’s inter-services public relations director general Lt Gen Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry said the agreement was “defensive” and “complementary” to the three countries’ existing alliances.

Article Title: Pakistan ministers warn of energy crisis; Shehbaz government struggles as fuel prices break records
Article Text:
Shehbaz ministers warn of energy crisis as Pakistan fuel prices surge

Fuel shock puts Shehbaz government under pressure

Pakistan is facing a widening energy crunch as disruptions around key Gulf shipping routes push up global oil prices, fuel costs surge and the government weighs measures to curb petroleum consumption.Pakistan’s Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif’s government is facing pressure on multiple fronts, with ministers warning about the impact of disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz and Bab El-Mandeb while trying to shield consumers from soaring fuel prices.Petrol prices were raised by PKR 4.10 per litre and high-speed diesel by PKR 6.41 per litre on Tuesday night, taking petrol to PKR 384.34 per litre and HSD to PKR 415.83 per litre.The sharp increases have raised concerns about how long Pakistan can absorb the impact of the global oil shock, with climate change minister Musadik Malik saying the government was trying to absorb part of the increase through its fuel relief scheme.Under the scheme, motorcyclists would receive subsidised petrol for up to five litres a week, while car owners would get relief on up to 10 litres every 10 days. Malik said the assistance would not fully offset the increase in fuel prices but represented the maximum burden the economy could currently absorb.Energy minister Awais Leghari also sounded the alarm over the supply situation, saying Pakistan had managed to keep its power plants running despite disruptions by maximising the use of domestic energy resources.In August, 72% of Pakistan’s electricity generation came from domestic sources, including hydropower, local coal, nuclear power, local gas, wind and solar, while 28% came from imported coal and RLNG.Leghari said disruptions to RLNG supplies had pushed spot cargo prices to $23.25 per MMBtu. Increased use of domestic gas for power generation helped Pakistan avoid buying more expensive RLNG, he said.Without the additional domestic gas, Pakistan could have faced another hour of load shedding, while greater reliance on furnace oil or imported RLNG could have increased consumer tariffs by around PKR 10.6 billion, according to the minister.As the energy crisis deepens, the government is considering ways to reduce petroleum consumption, including the possibility of a “smart lockdown”.Such measures were used during the peak of the US-Iran war, including a four-day working week and early closure of markets. Information minister Atta Tarar had also indicated that austerity measures could be brought back if the regional situation worsened.However, Malik rejected reports that a smart lockdown was currently being discussed, saying no such discussions had taken place.The government is simultaneously expanding its fuel relief programme. A National Steering Committee on Fuel Subsidy, chaired by deputy prime minister Ishaq Dar, has directed that payments to fuel stations be processed within 24 hours. The scheme, initially piloted in Islamabad, is being rolled out across Pakistan.The fuel shock is also creating political pressure. Jamaat-i-Islami has threatened nationwide demonstrations next week if fuel prices are not reduced.Pakistan has also switched to a daily petroleum pricing mechanism, introduced in July to replace the previous weekly system, as global oil prices became increasingly volatile amid geopolitical tensions.The crisis sharpens as Saudi Arabia has shut its East-West oil pipeline after it came under aerial attack, adding to concerns over global supplies.
Article Summary: Petrol prices were raised by PKR 4.10 per litre and high-speed diesel by 6.41. The sharp increases have raised concerns about how long Pakistan can absorb the impact of the global oil shock. The government is considering ways to reduce petroleum consumption, including the possibility of a ‘smart lockdown’

Article Title: 'Our father being slowly killed': Imran Khan's sons accuse Pakistan's Asim Munir of vendetta
Article Text:
Imran Khan's sons: Sulaiman Khan (left) and Kasim Khan (Photo: The Times)

The sons of jailed former Pakistan prime minister Imran Khan have accused army chief Asim Munir of pursuing a "personal vendetta" against their father, alleging that his prison conditions amount to mental and physical torture.Speaking to The Guardian, Kasim Khan, 27, and Sulaiman Khan, 29, said they were “deeply” concerned about the health of their 73-year-old father, who has been held at Adiala prison in Rawalpindi since his arrest in 2023.Khan is serving a 14-year sentence in a corruption case. His sons said they had not been allowed to speak to him for more than six months and had also been prevented from travelling from the UK to Pakistan to seek his release.The allegations come ahead of a Supreme Court ruling on Wednesday in a case alleging that the Pakistan government has failed to comply with a court order allowing Khan private hospital treatment for an eye condition and permitting family visits and communication.Sulaiman alleged that his father had been denied human contact, new books, access to family and an independent doctor. He also said Khan’s eye condition had been neglected for months, potentially resulting in severe loss of sight in one eye."It’s very clear this is being driven by personal grudge," Sulaiman told The Guardian, alleging that Khan was being treated harshly on Munir’s orders.Khan had reportedly demoted Munir during his tenure as prime minister, and tensions between the two were widely known. Munir became army chief in 2022, while Khan’s political conflict with the military establishment intensified.Kasim alleged that the family believed their father was being “slowly killed” in prison and said they feared restrictions on him could become harsher when international pressure eased.The allegations follow a recent dispute over Khan’s medical treatment. Last month, the Supreme Court ruled that he should be taken to a private hospital for treatment of a blood clot in a retinal vein. His family said the condition had severely affected the sight in his right eye.Khan was instead briefly taken to a government hospital, where he received injections before being declared fit to return to prison, according to The Guardian.The Pakistan government has rejected the allegations, calling them “fake propaganda”. It said Khan was being kept in adequate conditions and had access to home-cooked food, nuts, bottled water, exercise equipment, family visits and regular medical examinations.“The government of Pakistan categorically rejects allegations that the convicted prisoner is being subjected to punitive solitary confinement, cruelty or deprivation,” it said.The United Nations has previously said Khan’s prolonged detention violates international law, while the UN special rapporteur on torture has said his solitary confinement and detention conditions could amount to psychological torture.
Article Summary: Imran Khan is serving a 14-year sentence in a corruption case. His sons have accused army chief Asim Munir of pursuing a "personal vendetta" They say they have not been allowed to speak to him for more than six months. The Pakistan government has rejected the allegations.

Article Title: Pakistan military jets strike Kalat in fresh Balochistan attacks: Report
Article Text:
Balochistan: Pakistani aircraft reportedly conduct airstrikes in Kalat

Drone, helicopter attacks also reported

Pakistani military aircraft reportedly carried out airstrikes at two locations in Kalat on Monday, a day after a drone allegedly targeted a vehicle in Manguchar, according to a report by The Balochistan Post (TBP).A jet aircraft reportedly conducted an airstrike in the Chappar area of Kalat, where a powerful blast was heard. There was no immediate information about casualties or the extent of damage.Another explosion was reported near Took and Dasht-e-Goran. The exact location of the blast could not immediately be confirmed, though jet aircraft were reportedly seen flying over the area around the time of the explosion, news agency ANI cited.On Sunday, a drone reportedly targeted a vehicle in Manguchar. Gunship helicopters also allegedly shelled Rudeenjo and nearby areas for several hours on Sunday, while quadcopter attacks were reported from parts of the district.Communication disruptions and movement restrictions in the affected areas have made it difficult to independently verify the reports or obtain comprehensive details about casualties and damage, TBP said.The reported attacks come amid a series of military operations and aerial strikes across Balochistan in recent weeks, with several incidents triggering allegations of civilian casualties.
Article Summary: Pakistani military aircraft reportedly carried out airstrikes at two locations in Kalat on Monday. On Sunday, a drone allegedly targeted a vehicle in Manguchar. Gunship helicopters also allegedly shelled Rudeenjo and nearby areas for several hours on Sunday.

Article Title: Pak ups reward for Masood Azhar by PKR 20L ahead of FATF meet
Article Text: Taking its duplicity on combating terror to farcical levels, Pakistan's Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) has declared a reward of PKR 70 lakh on UN-designated terrorist Maulana Masood Azhar while calling him a "fugitive". The move comes ahead of the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) meeting next month.Pakistan had initially included Azhar in its 'red book' in 2021, setting a bounty of PKR 50 lakh. With apprehensions of being placed back on the FATF's 'grey list', Pakistan has now raised the reward by an additional PKR 20 lakh after five years.The move comes despite Islamabad's long-standing falsehood that Azhar escaped to Afghanistan and was no longer in the country. Even after key family members overseeing Jaish-e-Mohammed operations were eliminated in Operation Sindoor, Pakistan has remained unwilling to acknowledge his presence on its territory or extradite him to India. The assessment of Indian agencies is that he is based in the Sindh province but is often moved to different locations by the ISI to escape an assassination bid.Azhar, who is believed to have escaped the attack on the JeM's headquarters in Markaz Subhanallah, Bahawalpur, is wanted in India in connection with several attacks, including the 2019 Pulwama bombing in which 40 CRPF personnel were killed.Azhar's profile in the 'red book', which lists Pakistan's most-wanted fugitives and terrorists, doesn't mention any details including national ID card or passport number, place of birth, sect or any identification mark."The federal govt of Pakistan is offering a reward of Rs 70,00,000 for information directly leading to apprehension or conviction of Masood Azhar, the son of Khuda Baksh," it says.As it did in 2021, Pakistan has also maintained that the 26/11 Mumbai attack planners were not on its soil, as per the book. It has retained the profiles of 17 terrorists involved in the planning and financing of the Mumbai attacks, continued from 2021, but the photographs and details of two of the terrorists - Abdul Rehman and Muhammad Khan - have been removed this time. Khan had provided the boat used in the attack.The 'red book' in Pakistan is an official document published by law enforcement agencies to 'list and track' the country's most-wanted fugitives and high-profile terrorists.
Article Summary: Pakistan's Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) has declared a reward of PKR 70 lakh on UN-designated terrorist Maulana Masood Azhar. The move comes ahead of the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) meeting next month. Azhar is wanted in India in connection with several attacks, including the 2019 Pulwama bombing.

Article Title: Pakistan weighs austerity measures as US-Iran war drives up fuel prices
Article Text: Pakistan may bring back austerity measures to reduce fuel consumption as renewed fighting in West Asia drives up global oil prices, as news agency PTI cited Pak information minister Ataullah Tarar Monday.Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif has directed officials to examine which of the measures introduced earlier this year can be brought back, Tarar said at a press briefing attended by information technology minister Shaza Fatima Khawaja and petroleum minister Ali Pervaiz Malik."Austerity measures previously taken... are being reviewed to assess which of the previous measures need to be revived in the present situation," Tarar said.Pakistan had introduced the measures on March 9 as oil prices surged during the US-Iran war.The steps included halving fuel allowances for official vehicles, reducing lawmakers' salaries and allowing public sector employees to work from home for part of the week.The measures were withdrawn in June after the US and Iran entered a peace process. But renewed hostilities have once again pushed up international oil prices, putting pressure on fuel-importing countries such as Pakistan.Some restrictions, including shorter market hours, are already continuing, Tarar said.The government is facing the renewed pressure as petrol prices have climbed to PKR 375.82 per litre and high-speed diesel to PKR 403.32 per litre.To cushion the impact on smaller vehicle users, the government has announced a relief of Rs 100 per litre for motorcycles, rickshaws, Qingqi three-wheelers and vehicles with engine capacities of up to 800cc.Tarar said Sharif had asked deputy PM and foreign minister Ishaq Dar to make sure transport fares did not rise after the relief scheme was introduced.
Article Summary: Pakistan may bring back austerity measures to reduce fuel consumption as renewed fighting in West Asia drives up global oil prices. PM Shehbaz Sharif has directed officials to examine which of the measures introduced earlier this year can be brought back. Measures included halving fuel allowances for official vehicles, reducing lawmakers' salaries and allowing public sector employees to work from home.
